headline: High-risk overlap: shared filesystem and broad write/network privileges make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses shared memory by default; Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and ingest MCP/API content. If Devin consumes CrewAI outputs from a shared workspace or integration channel, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The interaction is plausible in default setups, though not proven documented.
conditions: IF CrewAI outputs are written into a workspace file that Devin later reads as task context
IF Devin ingests content from a shared integration channel without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in shared files
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Require human review before Devin acts on CrewAI-produced text

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and has broad network egress; Devin touches source code, issue trackers, chat, docs, and can write to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion. If both are pointed at the same repo or workspace, sensitive data can flow from CrewAI into Devin's broader integration surface and onward to third-party services. The shared-data path is plausible by default.
conditions: IF both agents are granted access to the same repository or workspace
IF Devin is connected to Slack, Jira, Notion, or GitHub write integrations while CrewAI processes sensitive crew inputs
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive test data
Remove Devin write scopes for the session
Use separate repos or directories per agent
Turn off network egress for CrewAI when handling secrets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the host filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Devin can write its cloud workspace, modify git state, and use MCP. If both are pointed at the same mutable repo or synced workspace, concurrent edits and git-state races can corrupt work or overwrite each other's changes. The profiles show overlapping write authority with no locking mechanism.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or shared directory
IF no external lock or merge gate serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or repos
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable Devin git writes during CrewAI runs
Require pull-request review before merges

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative intermediate results. Devin is an autonomous planner-executor with browser, shell, and write integrations, so it can act on those outputs. That creates a default pathway where CrewAI mistakes can cascade into Devin actions without verification, with potentially irreversible side effects.
conditions: IF Devin consumes CrewAI-produced plans, facts, or code without an explicit verification step
IF Devin is allowed to execute writes or external actions based on CrewAI output
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Devin acts
Require citations or tests for CrewAI outputs
Limit Devin to read-only review mode
Block external writes until human approval

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI is open-source and host-run, while Devin is closed-source and vendor-managed in a cloud workspace with integrations and retention-sensitive data classes like source code, chat, and issue trackers. If regulated or confidential data is processed, the pair can create residency and retention mismatches across the two operating models. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their combined deployment.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in Devin's cloud workspace
IF the operator requires a single retention or residency policy across both agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention and residency for each agent
Use separate environments for sensitive workloads
Review vendor terms before enabling integrations
